sum: Stellantis оставит свой исторический завод Mirafiori в Турине простаивающим в течение недели с 16 по 20 ноября, продлевая остановку производства Fiat 500 на пятую неделю подряд, согласно отчету Reuters, опубликованному в четверг, 12 ноября. Акции Stellantis торговались на Lang & Schwarz по 3,51 евро в 11:01 по центральноевропейскому времени в пятницу, 13 ноября.

FIOM-CGIL, FIM-CISL и UILM заявили, что рабочие, назначенные на производственные линии Fiat 500, останутся во временном отпуске в течение недели. Ожидается, что другие виды деятельности на объекте, включая операции со специальными автомобилями, RG Premium и Maserati, продолжатся.

Игорь Альбера из профсоюза FIM-CISL сообщил агентству Reuters, что длительные остановки отражают как нехватку компонентов, так и слабый спрос на Fiat 500. Представитель Stellantis заявил, что временные остановки на некоторых итальянских заводах могут продолжаться до ноября и декабря из-за нехватки поставщиков, затрагивающей компонент для блока управления двигателем N3 GSE. Компания еженедельно оценивает производственные графики, стремясь восстановить нормальную работу.

Это изменение актуально не только для Mirafiori, поскольку то же семейство двигателей также используется в Fiat Pandina. Повторяющиеся остановки увеличивают неопределенность в отношении использования заводов, планирования труда и поставок транспортных средств, хотя в отчете Reuters не содержится количественной оценки прямого влияния на прибыль Stellantis.

Альбера заявил, что отчет MF заслуживает доверия, поскольку прогнозирует, что до конца года осталось всего две производственные недели, а в 2026 году объем производства Mirafiori составит чуть более 50 000 автомобилей. Он добавил, что двух недель производства будет достаточно, чтобы покрыть текущий портфель заказов как на гибридную, так и на электрическую версии Fiat 500.

Для инвесторов это обновление добавляет операционный риск к повествованию о восстановлении Stellantis. Перебои в поставках могут ограничить выпуск даже при наличии заказов, в то время как отчет профсоюза указывает на отдельную проблему спроса. Таким образом, перед компанией стоит задача решить проблему доступности запчастей и продемонстрировать, что спрос на Fiat 500 может поддерживать более устойчивый ритм производства.

sum: BASF picked up a pair of SPE Automotive Innovation honours this week for plastic components developed with carmaking partners, though the recognition did nothing to shield the chemicals group's stock from a broad market downdraft. The shares shed 2.9% on Friday as a global retreat from AI and semiconductor names rippled through German equities, with no link established between the decline and the award announcements.

The Ludwigshafen-based company, working alongside Stellantis and L&L Products, took the SPE Automotive Innovation Award in the Chassis/Hardware category for a composite tunnel reinforcement used in the 2027 model-year Jeep Grand Cherokee. A second project earned the top prize: BASF, Toyota and Vuteq claimed the SPE Automotive Innovation Grand Award for the thermoplastic truck bed of the 2026 Toyota Tacoma, an application that also won in the Body Exterior category.

A third accolade went to BASF with Ford and Supavut Thailand in the Materials category, recognising door-handle trim on the 2026 Ford Everest. Together the three projects span different partners and vehicle applications, underscoring the group's reach across automotive supply chains.

The stock weakness had little to do with any of that. According to the Tagesschau, the worldwide selloff in AI and chip stocks weighed on the German market as a whole, and BASF was among the weakest performers in European chemicals during morning trading, dpa-AFX reported. Worries about the future momentum of AI investment drove selling pressure across sectors rather than any fresh operating news from BASF itself.

On the operating front, the picture is brighter. Roughly two weeks ago the group lifted its full-year 2026 forecast, now projecting EBITDA before special items of EUR 7.4bn to EUR 7.8bn, up from a previous range of EUR 6.9bn to EUR 7.7bn.
Third-quarter figures released on 28 October showed sales climbing 14% year on year to EUR 16.4bn, while EBITDA before special items rose 15% to EUR 1.6bn.

Beyond automotive and core chemicals, BASF has been rolling out new applications. On 30 October its trinamiX subsidiary and Eurofins Agro Testing unveiled a joint approach to mobile feed analysis for EuroTier 2026, combining NIR spectroscopy with calibration models.

EXEL Stock Slides After FDA Adds Three Months To Cancer Drug Review — William Blair Sees More Swings In Near Term
sum: Shares of Exelixis (EXEL) fell 2% on Friday after the company said U.S. regulators added three months to the review of its next cancer drug, but William Blair still sees a low chance of an outright rejection.

The Food and Drug Administration told Exelixis on Thursday that it had extended the review of a new drug application for zanzalintinib plus Roche’s Tecentriq in patients whose colorectal cancer has spread, the company said in a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission on Friday. The new target decision date is March 3, 2027. The old date was December 3, 2026. A March decision would push a possible U.S. launch out of this year and into 2027.

The FDA asked for more information and Exelixis sent updated safety and efficacy results, the company said. The agency treated that package as a major change to the application and extended its review period.

The FDA accepted Exelixis’s application in February for adults with metastatic colorectal cancer who had already received standard chemotherapy. Patients whose tumors lacked a common RAS mutation also had to have tried a separate targeted drug first.
The filing rests on STELLAR-303, a late-stage study that tested Exelixis’s oral drug with Tecentriq against Bayer’s Stivarga. In the full study population, patients on the combination lived longer.

Doubt remains because a second, pre-set test missed its mark. In June, Exelixis said patients without active liver tumors showed a similar trend but not a statistically clear survival win. Investors have worried the mixed result could slow the review, narrow the label, or invite extra questions. Friday’s filing did not say the new data requested by the FDA came from that subgroup.

William Blair said it was “surprised” by the three-month delay but still sees a low chance of an outright rejection, because the combination showed a survival benefit in the main study group. The firm said the extra wait should not materially cut the drug’s long-term sales, though the stock may swing more in the near term. It kept an ‘Outperform’ rating.

Dodge Is Back In NASCAR And All Is Well With The World
sum: There was so much news this week that I had to wait until Friday to write about the one story I personally cared about in The Morning Dump: Dodge is back in the top-level NASCAR Cup series. Yes, yes, yes, yes. America is so back, baby!

Other, less interesting people might argue that the news that former VW North America chief Pablo Di Si is getting the COO job here is the bigger Stellantis news, but nope, it’s the NASCAR thing. Oh, hey, remember when Audi announced a plant in Georgia, and it got all caught up in politics? Now that the elections are behind us, Audi is apparently looking to expand even more there than initially announced.
Remember Hertz? Hertz still exists, but it’s not going super well. Maybe they should rent V8-powered 911s? Those are fun.
Dodge And NASCAR Go Together Like Peanut Butter And Chocolate, Or A PB Cup And My Belly

The last year that Dodge ran in the top-level Cup series was in 2012, which was also the final outing of the 5th generation cars. They went out on top, with Brad Keselowski winning the championship. The then-Italian-American brand disinvested from NASCAR as it focused on other things. When FCA became Stellantis, it seemed even more remote that Dodge would return.

That all changed when the American arm of the company took over last year, and we were all treated to RAM running in the NASCAR truck series (you can watch our own Parker Kligerman racing tonight in a RAM). Rightly, everyone saw this as a prelude to the return of Dodge and its Charger to Cup.

Tim Kuniskis, head of American Brands, SRT Performance and Direct Connection division, Stellantis North America, shared the news during a sneak preview of the Stellantis display at the 2026 Specialty Equipment Market Association (SEMA) Show. For Dodge, the message is simple: gasoline-powered performance is back at the center of the brand, and Dodge is heading back to NASCAR Cup Series racing.

Stocks Plunge on an AI Selloff and Tesla Falls More Than 8%. What It Means for Car Buyers and Automakers
sum: Stocks sold off sharply Thursday as AI and chip stocks led Wall Street lower and erased the post-election rally. Intraday, the Nasdaq fell about 5%, the S&P 500 roughly 3% to 4% and the Dow more than 1,100 points, according to Yahoo Finance and Bloomberg. Tesla opened down more than 8%. The auto industry was already working through weaker consumer confidence and higher borrowing costs, so the question is how much a market slide adds.

Tesla trades more like a growth and tech stock than a traditional automaker, which is why it moves with the Nasdaq. Ford, GM and Stellantis have faced their own pressure. Stellantis shares fell 7% on Oct. 2 and 8% on Oct. 23 in separate sessions, and Ford and Stellantis each dropped about 4% in August after the White House set 50% auto tariffs on Canada.

Cox Automotive’s updated October estimate put the seasonally adjusted sales rate at 15.5 million, below its 16.1 million forecast. Volume came in around 1.324 million units, up 2.9% from a year earlier but under forecast. Cox cited weak stock market performance, election uncertainty, poor consumer confidence and rising loan rates, and said retail demand accounted for most of the shortfall because fleet sales rose nearly 6%. Cox also credited wealthier buyers and wider access to credit with keeping the market stronger than low confidence alone would suggest, and wealthier buyers are the group a falling stock market is most likely to affect.

The Manheim Used Vehicle Value Index stood at 207.4 in mid-October, up 0.7% from September on an adjusted basis and up 2.2% from a year earlier. Cox’s Jonathan Gregory said “supply, not demand, appears to be what slowed depreciation,” and described dealer demand as roughly flat. If buyers pull back further, flat demand leaves wholesale prices with little cushion.

Falling stock prices alone rarely change a car payment. Loan rates matter more, and the 10-year Treasury yield eased to about 4.84% from 4.90% on Thursday, according to Bloomberg. Buyers with a strong trade-in or cash may gain leverage if automakers add incentives to move retail inventory, though that usually takes weeks to show up. Buyers financing most of a purchase should watch rates and lender standards more than headlines.

sum: European stocks closed mixed on Wednesday (the 28th), as divergent third-quarter corporate earnings, a rebound in international oil prices of more than 1.7%, and the impending European Central Bank (ECB) rate decision kept trading sentiment cautious. The pan-European Stoxx Europe 600 index ended up 0.46 points, or 0.07%, at 644.14 points, marking a third consecutive session of gains after bulls and bears battled through the session and the index barely held above the flat line.

Among major regional markets, Germany's Frankfurt DAX index rose 0.44% to 25,704.02 points; the UK's FTSE 100 edged up 0.07% to 10,694.50 points; Italy's FTSE MIB gained 0.40% to 49,824.30 points; and France's CAC 40 slipped 0.18 points to 7,886.96 points. Spain's IBEX 35 index, weighed down by heavy selling in bank stocks, fell 1.45% to 18,883.50 points, the weakest performer among the five major markets.

Note: France's CAC 40 fell only marginally by 0.18 points on the day, a decline of less than 0.01%.

By sector, autos rose 1.33%, ranking as the center of buying interest among the 20 major sectors, driven mainly by multinational auto giant Stellantis. Bank stocks diverged markedly. sum: Stellantis ended another negative session on Wall Street on October 23, with STLA shares closing at $4.06, down 4.92%. The stock recovered part of its losses after falling as low as $3.92 during the session, but the picture since the start of 2026 remains bleak, with shares in the Antonio Filosa-led group down 62.7%.
Stellantis stock extends its decline as 2026 losses approach 63%

Compared with the U.S. intraday record high of $29.51 reached on March 25, 2024, the current price represents a decline of around 86.2%. In just over two and a half years, the stock has therefore fallen to less than one-seventh of the level it reached during that session.

Analyst downgrades and wider concerns about the automotive sector weighed on the latest trading day. HSBC cut its price target for Stellantis’ European shares from €4 to €3.30 while maintaining its Reduce rating. Volvo’s losses also sent the Swedish company’s stock down nearly 30%, adding pressure to shares of other automakers.

The weakness accumulated throughout the year comes as Stellantis works through a costly industrial overhaul. In February, the company announced €22.2 billion in charges related to the second half of 2025, covering changes to vehicle programs, the battery supply chain and warranty estimates. Filosa acknowledged that the company had previously overestimated the pace of electric vehicle adoption.

Around €6.5 billion of those charges will require cash payments over four years. Stellantis’ 2025 loss also led the company to suspend its dividend in 2026, leaving shareholders without a payout on top of the decline in the stock price.

Subsequent financial results showed improvement, although margins remained thin. Second-quarter revenue rose 13% to €43.5 billion, while net profit reached €293 million. Adjusted operating income margin stood at 1.8%, with Enlarged Europe still posting a loss on that measure.

sum: Traders on the Milan Stock Exchange popped the champagne just long enough to send Stellantis shares ticking up 1.71% following August’s Italian vehicle registration report. On paper, the figures look like a victory lap. The automotive giant posted a 6.2% surge in Italian registrations last month, nearly double the overall market’s modest 3.15% bump, lifting its domestic market share from 26.4% to 27.2%.

Zooming out to the first eight months of 2026, the victory lap gets even louder. Stellantis registered 341,225 vehicles in Italy between January and August, jumping 14% compared to the 299,264 units logged over the same stretch in 2025. That easily beat the broader Italian market’s 8.54% expansion, bumping Stellantis’s eight-month market share up to 30.2% from 28.7%.

Across major European markets, group registrations climbed 7% against a 5% industry benchmark, prompting casual observers to assume executive management was orchestrating an operational masterclass. Then the analysts at Intermonte ruined the party by reading the fine print.
Strip out the contributions from Chinese joint-venture partner Leapmotor, and Stellantis’s European growth suddenly collapses to an underwhelming 3.5%, sliding right behind the market average.

To make matters spicier, the sales mix looks like a balance-sheet headache. While passenger car registrations rose 11%, lucrative light commercial vehicles dropped 5%. Growth wasn’t driven by high-margin luxury nameplates either. Cheap Fiats and budget Citroëns carried the volume, while higher-value brands actively dragged down the spreadsheet.

As Equita dryly observed, Stellantis underperformed in France, and its Italian bragging rights depend entirely on counting Leapmotor’s imported hardware. Over in North America, the group managed to beat the market almost exclusively because Ram trucks continue to shoulder the load.

Yet despite the margin-squeezing product mix and mounting European geopolitical headwinds, analysts at Sim remain remarkably optimistic. They expect dealer shipments (sell-in) to outpace customer registrations in the third quarter as new models roll out, maintaining that Stellantis can still hit its mid-single-digit revenue growth targets for 2026.

Stock splits carry no fundamental change to a company’s value. Every shareholder receives more shares at a proportionally lower price, leaving total holdings unchanged. Recent mega-cap splits offer a clear lesson: underlying business performance drives returns, not the split mechanics.

Some investors might recall the company's unique car-vending machines that help drive brand awareness, provide unique user experiences, and give the company a brick-and-mortar footprint.

Carvana is now doing something interesting; it's buying new car dealerships. On March 3, it took yet another step forward, buying its sixth new car dealership that more closely connects the used car retailer with Stellantis and new car sales.

The most recent purchase was a Stellantis dealership west of Boston, renamed as Carvana Chrysler-Dodge-Jeep-Ram (CDJR). Carvana previously purchased five other CDJR stores spread between California, Arizona, and Texas. Carvana hasn't given specifics behind its strategy, but it's easy to see the potential gains. Buying physical dealerships will shift the used car retailer to a hybrid model incorporating online sales with local and physical original equipment manufacturer (OEM)-certified inventory.

Beyond that, the strategy will also secure a backlog of used car inventory from trade-ins and off-lease vehicles, boost margins with new car sales, and serve consumers who still want to test drive or pick vehicles up in person. Furthermore, the acquisitions, which are largely in California, Arizona, and Texas, appear to be located to strengthen and extend their national distribution network, which has a heavier East Coast footprint.

The broader strategy makes a lot of sense for the company and its investors, especially when done at a calculated pace -- rather than the rapid and costly expansion that caused the business some difficulties in the past. However, one question remains.

This development aligns with reports from news agency Bloomberg, which, citing insider sources, claims that Stellantis is now also planning to exit its battery joint venture with the South Korean company Samsung SDI. The venture is currently constructing two battery cell factories in Kokomo, Indiana, USA, and already operates a production facility for stationary battery energy storage systems (BESS) at the site.

Stellantis, a conglomerate encompassing 14 brands such as Fiat, Opel, and Peugeot in Europe, and Chrysler, Jeep, and Ram in the US, is currently exploring options to withdraw from the joint venture. However, no final decision has been made. An exit could prove costly for Stellantis, potentially leading to further write-downs or penalty payments to its partner Samsung SDI. After all, Stellantis intended to use the cells produced at the facility for its electric vehicles (EVs), though this would not necessarily be ruled out if the plant were to have a different ownership structure in the future.

It is not yet certain that Samsung SDI will take over Stellantis’s shares—as LG Energy Solution did with NextStar Energy for a symbolic price of just 100 US dollars. According to Bloomberg’s sources, Stellantis might also sell its stake to a third party. “We continue to hold discussions with Samsung regarding the future of our joint venture, StarPlus Energy,” Stellantis stated in an email to Bloomberg, while the news agency has yet to receive an official statement from Samsung SDI.

What the automaker delivered alongside that move was a set of third-quarter 2026 US delivery figures that tell a story far more complicated than the headline number suggests.

On the surface, the US volume looks reassuring. Stellantis moved 324,277 vehicles in the third quarter, essentially flat against the 324,825 units of the prior-year period. For the first nine months of the year, US sales climbed 3% to 958,463 units.

The composition of those sales, however, is where the trouble starts. Ram was the standout performer, with deliveries jumping 29% to 134,072 vehicles. The Ram 1500 alone surged 73%, pushing Jeep out of the top spot in the group's internal brand ranking for the first time.

That milestone cuts both ways. Jeep — the group's most profitable nameplate and, for years, the dependable earnings engine in North America — slumped 20% to 128,542 units. When the highest-margin brand loses that much ground and cheaper models are left to fill the gap, the pressure on the group's margin profile becomes difficult to ignore.

On the other side of the Atlantic, the picture is brighter but not uniform. Italian registrations rose 12.6% in September to 38,704 vehicles, lifting the group's market share to 27.8%. In France, passenger-car volumes excluding the Leapmotor brand advanced 6.7%.

Those gains come against a backdrop of persistent operational friction. Temporary production stoppages hit French plants including Sochaux and Rennes in October due to high-voltage battery shortages, while shift cancellations at Mirafiori in Italy underscored that supply chains remain far from smooth. The market is demanding rapid progress on electrification; logistics are still slowing the lines.

sum: Shares of automaker Stellantis plunged 27% in European trading on Friday, after the company said it expects to take a 22-billion-euro ($26 billion) hit from a business reset and hinted at a pull-back from its electrification push.
In Milan, the company's Italian shares fell 25% Friday. On Wall Street, the transatlantic firm's New York-listed stock plummeted 23%.
Other French auto stocks also fell Friday morning, with Valeo and Forvia both down more than 1.2% and Renault sliding 2%.

"The charges announced today largely reflect the cost of over-estimating the pace of the energy transition that distanced us from many car buyers' real-world needs, means and desires," said Stellantis CEO Antonio Filosa in a statement.
"They also reflect the impact of previous poor operational execution, the effects of which are being progressively addressed by our new Team."

Going forward, Stellantis said it would remain at the forefront of EV development, but said its own electrification journey would continue at "a pace that needs to be governed by demand rather than command."

sum: Stellantis is reshaping its manufacturing footprint in Mexico, reallocating production to its Saltillo and Toluca complexes and confirming at least 13 product launches for 2026, including 11 with some level of electrification. The automaker also plans to introduce the Chinese EV brand Leapmotor to the Mexican market, positioning both moves within a broader industrial restructuring strategy.
“This is only the beginning of what will happen in Mexico. What matters is what comes next,” said Daniel González, CEO, Stellantis Mexico.

The decision comes as several automakers adjust their footprints in the country. General Motors has shifted part of its production to the United States, Nissan will close two facilities in Aguascalientes and Morelos, and brands including BYD and Tesla have delayed or canceled planned projects. Stellantis’ new allocations break with this trend and increase activity in two of its core manufacturing hubs.

In Saltillo, production has begun on the RAM 1500, a full-size pickup that competes directly with the Chevrolet Silverado built in Silao. The shift reinforces Saltillo’s role as a central manufacturing base for RAM in North America.

Toluca is slated for a more diversified program. The plant will produce the sixth-generation Jeep Cherokee hybrid—the first hybrid version in the model’s history—as well as the Recon, an electric vehicle aligned with Stellantis’ Dare Forward 2030 global strategy. These assignments join existing production of the Compass and the Wagoneer S, which entered assembly last year.

With the added models, Stellantis says employment stability has strengthened across both facilities. The company reports that its expanded Mexican portfolio has already generated 5,000 new jobs. “We have eight plants in the country, two main complexes, 13,000 people in the plants and 17,000 in total. This shows a company that is betting on Mexico and believes in Mexico,” González said. The automaker also posted its strongest November sales results in recent years.
As part of its broader strategy, Stellantis will also bring Leapmotor to Mexico.

Trump says he will roll back fuel efficiency standards for vehicles
sum: President Donald Trump on Wednesday said his administration would "reset" fuel efficiency standards for passenger cars in an effort to put a lid on rising auto prices, as the administration battles inflation and an affordability crisis.
The previous rules, which sought to lower carbon emissions, “put tremendous upward pressure on car prices,” Trump said in the Oval Office.
The president is under political pressure to address affordability concerns after Democrats swept major races last month, fueled by voters' frustration with rising prices.

Overall inflation, as measured by the consumer price index, has risen every month since Trump announced sweeping tariffs on imported goods, including automobiles and car parts, among other items. Food prices have also been rising this year. In early November, the White House announced cuts to dozens of tariffs in a move aimed at cutting food prices.

The average new vehicle price in October surged to an all-time high, above $50,000 for the first time ever, according to Kelley Blue Book. However, KBB said that "despite higher prices, retail sales continue to maintain a healthy pace."
"The $20,000-vehicle is now mostly extinct, and many price-conscious buyers are sidelined or cruising in the used-vehicle market," Cox Automotive analyst Erin Keating said in October.

The Department of Transportation says the proposal will "save the American people $109 billion" or $1,000 on the average cost of a new vehicle, but it's unclear how fast prices could fall. The updated standards still must go through a formal rulemaking process before being finalized, likely in 2026.
